provenance.text: A host parameter is a place-holder in an SQL statement that is filled in using one of the sqlite3_bind_XXXX() interfaces. Many SQL programmers are familiar with using a question mark ("?") as a host parameter. SQLite also supports named host parameters prefaced by ":", "$", or "@" and numbered host parameters of the form "?123".
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: A "variable" or "parameter" token specifies a placeholder in the expression for a value that is filled in at runtime using the sqlite3_bind() family of C/C++ interfaces. Parameters can take several forms:
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: Each host parameter in an SQLite statement is assigned a number. The numbers normally begin with 1 and increase by one with each new parameter. However, when the "?123" form is used, the host parameter number is the number that follows the question mark.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: ?NNN A question mark followed by a number NNN holds a spot for the NNN-th parameter. NNN must be between 1 and SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: A consequence of this is that if the WAL file contains more than read-mark[N] frames (if mxFrame>read-mark[N] for any read-mark for which WAL_READ_LOCK(N) is held by another process), then the checkpoint cannot run to completion.
provenance.title: walformat

provenance.text: A question mark that is not followed by a number creates a parameter with a number one greater than the largest parameter number already assigned.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: To prevent excessive memory allocations, the maximum value of a host parameter number is SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER, which defaults to 999 for SQLite versions prior to 3.32.0 (2020-05-22) or 32766 for SQLite versions after 3.32.0.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: The maximum host parameter number can be lowered at run-time using the sqlite3_limit(db,SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER,size) interface.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: SQLite allocates space to hold all host parameters between 1 and the largest host parameter number used.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: If this means the parameter number is greater than SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER, it is an error.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: But because it is easy to miscount the question marks, the use of this parameter format is discouraged.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: Were it to do so, it would overwrite content that the process holding the lock was expecting to be able to read out of the main database file.
provenance.title: walformat

provenance.text: Hence, an SQL statement that contains a host parameter like ?1000000000 would require gigabytes of storage.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: When a writer wants to reset the WAL, it must ensure that there are no locks on WAL_READ_LOCK(N) for N>0 because such locks indicate that some other connection is still using the current WAL file and a WAL reset would delete content out from those other connections.
provenance.title: walformat

provenance.text: This parameter format is provided for compatibility with other database engines.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: SQLite limits the depth of recursion of triggers in order to prevent a statement involving recursive triggers from using an unbounded amount of memory.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: A string constant is formed by enclosing the string in single quotes ('). A single quote within the string can be encoded by putting two single quotes in a row - as in Pascal. C-style escapes using the backslash character are not supported because they are not standard SQL.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: When a checkpoint runs, if it sees a lock on WAL_READ_LOCK(N), then it must not move WAL content into the main database for more than the first read-mark[N] frames.
provenance.title: walformat

provenance.text: BLOB literals are string literals containing hexadecimal data and preceded by a single "x" or "X" character. Example: X'53514C697465'
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: This could easily overwhelm the resources of the host machine.
provenance.title: limits

provenance.text: Programmers are encouraged to use one of the symbolic formats below or the ?NNN format above instead.
provenance.title: lang expr

provenance.text: It is ok for a WAL reset to occur if other connections are holding WAL_READ_LOCK(0) because by holding WAL_READ_LOCK(0), those other connections are promising not to use any content from the WAL.
provenance.title: walformat
